A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RETRACEQA and provide readable main text, tables, figures, mathematical notation, and Appendices A–F. Matching relocated and renumbered material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotations of 2,421 reasoning traces, evaluations of PRMs and LLM judges, and downstream experiments with seven SLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains the original annotation results, judge evaluations, and downstream SLM experiments, including the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 and Appendix D refine the annotation method from overlapping error definitions into an ordered, mutually exclusive decision rule: misinterpretation, hallucination, then reasoning. Trace generation, automated judging, and PRM scoring procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CommonsenseQA, OpenBookQA, QASC, and StrategyQA for the same commonsense reasoning tasks, retaining reference-free, reference-based, and downstream evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The same five PRMs and eight LLM judges participate in corresponding comparisons in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3. The seven downstream SLMs are also unchanged; the added Pisano and Navigli citation introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported annotation protocol now prescribes category precedence and reserves reasoning errors for correctly grounded, factually correct premises, replacing the earlier overlapping criteria. The PDFs do not establish reannotation or experimental reruns. Sample counts, splits, decoding settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The qualitative diagnosis of the salt-and-ice example is revised from hallucination to faulty inference in Figure 1 and Section 3.5. The six other tabulated examples, error-position analysis, and individual-model analysis are retained; their redistribution does not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three annotators independently labeling the same-sized agreement subset: 100 instances, with 25 per dataset. Fleiss’s kappa changes from 84.4% to the equivalent rounded 0.84. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Figure 1 changes the example’s reported error category from Hallucination to Reasoning. All numerical entries in the benchmark statistics and main performance tables remain unchanged after matching v1 Tables 1–4 to v2 Tables 2–5; the retained analytical plots also show the same results.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same formal earliest-error identification task and index conventions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims remain: a commonsense reasoning-trace benchmark, correct answers despite flawed reasoning, inflated answer-only scores, difficulty localizing errors, and weak transfer of mathematical PRMs.

C2.justification: v2 adds a primary-cause explanation separating grounding, factual-content, and inference failures, and explains how hierarchical labeling reduces ambiguity. Its salt example now explicitly distinguishes a correct factual premise from an invalid deduction. Broader result interpretations and the English-language and domain limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a benchmark, code, and data release link; identifies the annotators as paper authors; and documents a single-newline fallback when double-newline segmentation is unavailable. The fallback is newly documented, without evidence that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 adds Pisano and Navigli (2026) concerning extensions to PRMs’ logical capabilities. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Consolidating the two Tyen entries merges publication and preprint references to the same work.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the annotation taxonomy in Section 3.5 and Appendix D and revise Appendix C around relocated examples. Other edits polish wording, standardize error-category terminology, and update affiliation and equal-contribution information. The overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised, and a new Figure 2 summarizes existing error-category distributions as a pie chart. v1 Table 7 is split between v2’s main-text Table 1 and appendix Table 8, with revised highlighting. Existing result tables and analytical plots are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the annotation rules more operational, corrects the illustrated error diagnosis, brings representative examples into the main text, and supplies resource-access information. These improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish reannotation under the revised rules, limiting the demonstrated improvement in empirical reliability.
